cloze.pt: A {mulher} de vermelho é a Ana.
cloze.en: The woman in red is Ana.
Two women went into the shop.
There are two months until summer.
The loaves are in the oven.
The hotel is near the beach.
The hotels are full in August.
I caught the eight o'clock train.
The dog is a loyal animal.
The farm animals wake up early.
I need a sheet of paper.
The papers are on the table.
I left my mobile at home.
We have been friends for years.
I am going to the market.

cloze.pt: O que {fazes} ao fim de semana?
cloze.en: What do you do at the weekend?
Do you know how to cook?
I see the sea from the window.
Are you watching the film today?
He puts the book on the shelf.

entries.en: to stay, to become, to be located

cloze.en: They eat a lot of fish.
She prefers to stay at home.
All the possible scenarios were studied.

entries.en: to him, to her, to you

cloze.en: Thank you very much for your help.

ser_estar.note: permanent location → ficar (PT prefers it to estar here)

ser_estar.en: The house is made of wood.

ser_estar.note: when an event takes place → ser
estar a + infinitive is the PT progressive
asking where a fixed thing is → ficar
a judgement about the thing itself → ser

ser_estar.en: I stayed at home all day.

por_para.en: I study in order to learn.
It was made by an artist.
I swapped the car for a bicycle.
We paid twenty euros a night.
I left because of the noise.

por_para.pt: A carta é {para} a minha mãe.
por_para.en: The letter is for my mother.
I sold the car for little money.
He studied to be a doctor.

personal_inf.en: Before we leave, close the window.
personal_inf.note: antes de + personal infinitive, subject nós

personal_inf.en: It's better for us to go now.

personal_inf.note: depois de + personal infinitive, subject vocês

personal_inf.en: For you to be happy, you need to rest.
personal_inf.note: para + personal infinitive; ser is regular here — seres, not fores

personal_inf.en: I brought the book for you to read.
personal_inf.note: purpose with a different subject → personal infinitive

personal_inf.en: It's important that we study together.
In case there are problems, call me.
personal_inf.note: third person singular, so no ending is added

personal_inf.en: Despite it being cold, we went out.
Before you eat, wash your hands.
It was difficult for us to find the house.

fut_subj.pt: Se {formos} à praia, levamos o guarda-sol.
fut_subj.en: If we go to the beach, we'll take the parasol.
fut_subj.note: future subjunctive of ir is FORMOS; the personal infinitive would be irmos

fut_subj.en: When it's your birthday, we'll celebrate.
fut_subj.note: future subjunctive fizeres, not the personal infinitive fazeres

fut_subj.en: When you're ready, let us know.
As soon as we know, we'll say.
If we speak slowly, he understands.
fut_subj.note: falar is regular, so the two forms are identical — this is why they get confused
chegar is regular: identical to the personal infinitive

false_friend.en: This cake has a strange taste.
false_friend.note: Spanish exquisito means delicious; PT esquisito means odd
PT embaraçada means embarrassed, not pregnant

false_friend.en: I work in an office in the centre.
false_friend.note: PT oficina is a workshop or garage

false_friend.en: I left the waiter a tip.
false_friend.note: PT propina is a tuition fee
PT largo means wide, not long

false_friend.en: There is a lot of dust on the shelf.
We are having dinner at eight.
false_friend.note: Spanish cena is dinner; PT cena is a scene
one l in Portuguese, two in Spanish

false_friend.en: She was embarrassed by the question.
false_friend.note: the same trap run the other way round

false_friend.pt: Preciso de uma {borracha} para apagar isto.
false_friend.en: I need an eraser to rub this out.
false_friend.note: PT borracha is rubber, an eraser

false_friend.en: I waited a while at the door.
false_friend.note: Spanish rato is a while; PT rato is a mouse
